title: Communication and Personality Development
summary: Communication (Latin communis, 'to share') is the act of conveying information to create mutual understanding; it needs a sender, a message and a receiver. Newman and Summer: an exchange of facts, ideas, opinions or emotions by two or more persons. Features: it involves at least two persons, it is incomplete until the receiver understands and gives feedback, its purpose is understanding and it is continuous. Process: sender, message, encoding, channel (medium), receiver, decoding and feedback. Barriers: noise, distance, information overload (e.g. a hotel receptionist taking over 20 calls in five minutes), language and an unfamiliar medium.

Advantages: immediate feedback, dialogue, fast, economical and flexible. Disadvantages: less reliable and open to misunderstanding, no record or reference, unsuitable for lengthy messages, influenced by the behaviour of sender and receiver, and high chance of distortion. Seven Cs: clear, concise, complete (five Ws), correct, concrete, courteous and candid. A good presentation: decide the topic, collect material, prepare and revise the draft, insert graphics, make a final draft, practise and present; know your audience, be concise, use short simple words, keep eye contact, look calm and smile.

A meeting is a get-together of a group to discuss a specific task. Objectives: to inform and explain, understand the situation, get feedback, exchange ideas, persuade members to accept changes, resolve conflicts and create a positive attitude. Convening a meeting has three steps: notice (date, time, place, issue), agenda (list of topics) and minutes (decisions recorded). Facing an interview: pre-plan, introduce yourself and shake hands, minimise distractions (switch off the phone), keep eye contact, frame answers positively, avoid jargon and never speculate.

Advantages: taken seriously, suitable for long messages, provides a record, accurate, can reach many people at once and gives clear guidelines. Disadvantages: time-consuming and costly, no immediate feedback, rigid and impersonal, drafting errors cause misunderstanding and secrecy is hard to keep. Oral vs written: oral is verbal, quick, easy to keep secret, better for short messages and gives no record; written is in words, takes time, hard to keep secret, better for long messages and gives a record. Seven Cs of written communication: concise, clarity, completeness, consideration, courtesy, correctness and concreteness. Principles of effective writing: unity, coherence, avoid jargon, accuracy and briefness. A business letter has: heading, date, reference, inside address, attention line, salutation, subject, body, complimentary close, signature and enclosure.

Customer care means systems that maximise customer satisfaction. Factors: understanding needs, matching the product or service, value for money, keeping customers informed, reliable order fulfilment, after-sales service, handling complaints, feedback and loyalty schemes, and the professionalism of staff. Loyalty schemes give discounts, extra goods or prizes (a travel agency may offer free local transport with deluxe hotel stays). Complaints should be handled courteously, sympathetically and swiftly: listen, stay calm, do not take it personally, record details, handle written complaints immediately, offer repair, replacement or refund, follow up and report back.

Personality (Latin persona, a theatre mask) is the combination of stable physical and mental characteristics that give an individual identity. Determinants: heredity, environment and situation. MBTI traits: extroversion vs introversion, sensing vs intuition, thinking vs feeling (thinking: logic; feeling: personal values) and judging vs perceiving (judging: structured; perceiving: flexible). Extroverts are sociable and assertive and are energised by people; introverts are quiet and shy and recharge alone. Big Five: openness to experience, conscientiousness (self-discipline, organised), extroversion, agreeableness (compassionate, cooperative) and emotional stability (tendency to experience unpleasant emotions easily).

A team is a group with complementary skills committed to a common purpose. Types: problem-solving (5–12 employees), self-managed (10–15), cross-functional (same level, different areas; task forces and committees) and virtual teams. Team building is a formal activity to improve a team's functioning. Steps: value each member's ideas, be aware of unspoken feelings, communicate clearly, encourage trust and cooperation and information sharing, delegate problem-solving, facilitate communication, have a clear goal, set ground rules, arrive at consensus and encourage listening and brainstorming. Tuckman's four stages: forming, storming, norming and performing.

sa: Describe the three steps in the process of convening a meeting.
(i) Notice: it tells members the date, time, place and issue. (ii) Agenda: a list of topics to be discussed, sent to members. (iii) Minutes: the decisions and conclusions recorded after discussion.
Distinguish between oral and written communication (three points).

(i) Oral messages are spoken and quick; written messages take time. (ii) Oral gives immediate feedback but no record; written gives a record and reference. (iii) Oral suits short messages and secrecy; written suits long messages and is precise.
Explain the seven Cs of written communication (three of them with meaning).

(i) Clarity: a clear objective and simple words. (ii) Completeness and conciseness: answer what, who, when, why and where briefly. (iii) Courtesy, consideration, correctness and concreteness: friendly 'you-attitude', correct facts and specific statements.
How should a tourism professional handle customer complaints? (three points)

(i) Listen sympathetically, stay calm and do not take it personally. (ii) Record the details and deal with written complaints at once. (iii) Offer repair, replacement or refund, follow up and report back with a solution.
Explain the personality traits of the Big Five model (three points).

(i) Openness to experience and conscientiousness (creative and curious; disciplined, organised). (ii) Extroversion and agreeableness (sociable; compassionate and cooperative). (iii) Emotional stability: the degree of control over unpleasant emotions.
la: Explain the role of written communication in tourism in six points.

(i) It is taken seriously and provides records. (ii) It suits long messages such as itineraries and brochures. (iii) It gives clear guidelines for staff and tourists. (iv) It reaches many persons at once. (v) Letters, memos, reports and manuals make business accurate. (vi) The seven Cs make it effective and correct format keeps it professional.

or: Explain the steps for building an effective team.

(i) Consider every member's ideas valuable. (ii) Be aware of unspoken feelings and communicate clearly. (iii) Encourage trust, cooperation and information sharing. (iv) Delegate problem-solving and facilitate communication. (v) Set a clear goal and ground rules. (vi) Establish a method for consensus and encourage listening and brainstorming.

la: How to face an interview? Explain in six points.

(i) Plan and rehearse with a friend. (ii) Be in control: introduce yourself and shake hands first. (iii) Minimise distractions such as the phone. (iv) Keep eye contact to look confident. (v) Frame answers positively and avoid jargon. (vi) Never speculate; if you do not know, say so and promise to find out.
Explain the process of communication and the barriers to it, in six points.

(i) The sender has a message. (ii) Encoding turns it into symbols. (iii) The channel carries it to the receiver. (iv) The receiver decodes it. (v) Feedback completes the process. (vi) Barriers are noise, distance, information overload, language and an unfamiliar medium.
Explain customer care management in six points.

(i) It is the system to maximise customer satisfaction. (ii) Understand needs and match products to them. (iii) Give value for money and reliable service. (iv) Gather feedback and keep customers informed. (v) Use loyalty schemes such as discounts and cards. (vi) Handle complaints courteously, sympathetically and swiftly.
